**Pick a power bank under 100 Wh, and keep it in your carry-on.** That matters more than the brand. Among the products in my search results, the best fit is the **Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)**. I only found this one product, so I can't say it beats every other bank.

## Why the Baseus Blade H1 fits
- **Airline-legal size:** It's about 74 Wh, under the 100 Wh limit. ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah))
- **Laptop-capable:** It has 100 W USB-C output, so one bank can charge a laptop and a phone. It also has 2× USB-C and 2× USB-A ports and pass-through charging.
- **Flat and light:** It measures 134 × 134 × 18 mm and weighs about 451 g.
- **Price and terms:** $89.99 at Baseus's US store (verified 2026-10-21), with a 24-month warranty and a 7-day return window.
- **Caveat:** Baseus doesn't publish per-port wattage when several devices charge at once.

**Buy:** [Baseus Blade H1 at Baseus's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). This is an affiliate link, so the listing site earns a commission at no cost to you.

## Rules to know before you fly
- **Carry-on only.** Power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the bank out and keep it with you. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **100 Wh limit per battery.** With airline approval you can bring up to two larger ones (101–160 Wh). To check a bank's rating, multiply volts by amp-hours. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- **Protect the terminals.** Use the original packaging, tape, or a pouch.
- **Airlines can be stricter.** Southwest, for example, limits each customer to **one power bank** as of April 20, 2026. It must stay out of the overhead bin and can't be charged from in-seat power. If you use it onboard, it must be visible, not inside a bag. ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters))
- **Check your airline's policy** before you go. The FAA and IATA both say rules vary. ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))

If you only need to top up a phone, a smaller 10,000 mAh bank is lighter and easily passes any airline's limits. Tell me your devices and budget and I can narrow it down.
